answer: For standard retail claims, you must submit the main reimbursement claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2]. For Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [5]. Note that an archived 2024 timeline document listed a 15-day deadline [3].
The room rent limit on the Aurora Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

For standard retail plans, pre-existing diseases generally carry a 36-month waiting period unless Aurora explicitly waives it in writing on the policy schedule [3][5]. Under the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the pre-existing disease waiting period is reduced to 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][5].

Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026 [1]. Because hospitals join and leave the network continuously, the authoritative list is available via the hospital locator in the Aurora app and portal [1].

Under the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. A claim does not reduce the accumulated bonus; it only stops accumulation for that year [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment [1]. Infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed as permanent treatment-related exclusions [1].
Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

Across all Aurora Health plans, road ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Gold plan provides air ambulance cover up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, and there is no separate waiting period for it [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. A new policyholder may cancel within 15 days of receiving the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. Upon cancellation during this period, the policyholder receives a refund of the premium less proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
Completing an annual health check-up earns 150 wellness points [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation because of technological advance, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
For a cashless emergency admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a TPA [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, not everything will be paid [5]. Under a Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2%, which is ₹10,000 per day [1][2]. Because a ₹15,000 room exceeds this limit, an eligibility ratio of 0.667 is applied, leading to proportionate deductions across various billed expenses [1][5].

Dependent parents can be added under the Silver plan (at an extra premium), Gold plan, and Platinum plan, but are not permitted under the Bronze plan [1]. When a parent is added, the policy premium is determined by the age of the eldest covered member, which often makes the floater more expensive than an individual senior-citizen policy for that parent [4].
